input.content:
# The festival finder

Stage 1 of the [data lifecycle](../../docs/data-lifecycle.md): the list of festivals we know
about, and the method for finding more. A festival qualifies for the site only when it
publishes a detailed per-session schedule (every show, screening, talk or race with its
date, start time and venue), so the finder records that for every festival it considers.

How a run works is the `festival-finder` skill; the `festival-finder` task runs it monthly.

## The two lists, and why they only grow

| file | holds | grows by |
|---|---|---|
| `sources.toml` | where to look: aggregators, platforms, organisers, seed lists, search queries | every route that surfaced a candidate, and every lesson about using one |
| `candidates.toml` | every festival considered, qualifying or not | every festival a run checks |
| `runs/<date>.md` | one log per run: scope, yield per source, the searches that found nothing | one file per run |

Nothing is ever deleted from either list. A source that stops answering becomes `blocked`
or `dead` with a `note`; a festival that does not qualify becomes `rejected` with a
`reason`. Both stay, because the next run needs to know what was tried as much as what
worked. `finder.py --growth <ref>` fails a change that drops an entry.

## `sources.toml`

```toml
[[source]]
id = "indico"                  # lowercase-hyphen slug, what candidates' found_via names
name = "Indico"
category = "platform"          # aggregator | platform | organiser | seed-list | search-query | technique
url = "https://indico.cern.ch" # required except for search-query and technique
kinds = ["academic"]           # registry kinds, or ["any"]
regions = ["world", "IL"]      # ISO country codes, or "world"
per_session = "yes"            # does a hit imply a per-session schedule? yes | partial | no
machine_readable = "…"         # optional: the export endpoint pattern
how = "…"                      # what the next run needs to use it: queries, filters, traps
status = "active"              # active | blocked | dead (the last two say why in note)
note = "…"                     # optional
added = "2026-09-29"
checked = "2026-09-29"         # when a run last used it
```

## `candidates.toml`

```toml
[[candidate]]
id = "isfn-annual-meeting"     # the festival, not an edition
name = "…"
kind = "academic"              # a registry kind
subtypes = ["academic-neuroscience"]   # optional, as festival.toml's
country = "IL"
city = "Eilat"
site = "https://…"
programme = "https://…"        # optional: the per-session programme page
next_first = "2026-12-07"      # optional: the next edition, when known
next_last = "2026-12-09"
schedule = "published"         # published | partial | expected | none | unknown
schedule_evidence = "…"        # optional: one concrete session with date, time and room
platform = "eventact"          # optional: what hosts the programme
status = "candidate"           # candidate | watch | adopted | rejected
festival_id = "…"              # adopted only: the id under scraper/festivals/
reason = "…"                   # watch and rejected: why
recheck = "2026-11-01"         # watch only: when to look again
found_via = ["ortra-eventact"] # source ids
checked = "2026-09-29"
```

Every festival registered under `scraper/festivals/` has an `adopted` candidate, so this
list is the whole set of festival pointers. `finder.py --check` holds that and every field
above; `scripts/verify.sh` runs it.

```
python3 scraper/finder/finder.py --report
python3 scraper/finder/finder.py --check --growth origin/main
```

entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

Based on the search results, I found information about the Israel Institute for Advanced Studies (IIAS) in Jerusalem. The Israel Institute for Advanced Studies (IIAS) was established by the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in 1975 as a self-governing body, whose mission is to create multidisciplinary learning communities of academics.

Regarding their 2026-2027 programs, proposals may be submitted for a five-month residency starting February 1, 2027 until June 30, 2027, and the IIAS invites scholars from Israel and abroad to submit Research Group (RG) proposals for the 2027-2028 academic year. Research proposals may be submitted by initiator(s) affiliated with any academic institution in Israel or abroad. Proposals may cover any research topic from all disciplines including interdisciplinary research, and must seek to be innovative with potential impact on their research field.

Additionally, along with selected individual fellows and collaborative Research Groups, the Institute annually hosts six Advanced Schools as well as many conferences.

For more detailed and current information about specific conferences scheduled for 2026-2027, I recommend visiting the IIAS website directly at iias.huji.ac.il or contacting them at +972 (0) 2 658 6931.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about the Clashfinder API and the `authPublicKey` parameter:

## authPublicKey Overview

The `authPublicKey` is a code generated by taking an sha256 hash of your username, private key and some optional parameters. Your account password does not affect the public key.

## API Parameters

API calls can have optional parameters that are encoded in the publicKey, so a public key is only valid for a specific set of parameters. The optional parameters include:

- **authParam** (optional, letters, numbers, hyphens and underscores only) - An additional parameter to include in the hash, for example to provide API calls for different people with unique public keys

- **authValidUntil** (optional, yyyymmddhhmmss) - A date and time that the public key will expire, with dates and times in UTC

## Authentication Requirements

All calls to the clashfinder API now require simple authentication, and a free user account will be required to use the API.

For more detailed API documentation, you can visit the official Clashfinder API page at https://clashfinder.com/pages/api/

## API Authentication

You will need to include an x-api-key header to authenticate your requests; you can acquire an API key from your API keys page. Alternatively, you can pass an api_key parameter set to your API key if you're unable to modify HTTP headers.

## Event Buckets and Events

Event buckets are collections of related events, passes, and attendees, and an event bucket can represent anything from a film festival to an opera season.

## API Endpoints and JSON Format

You can query catalog content using the endpoint: GET https://api.eventive.org/watch/catalog?event_bucket=EVENT_BUCKET_ID

You can retrieve virtual screenings and films for an event bucket, and filter the list of virtual screenings/films returned using a variety of parameters.

The API returns JSON responses that include event and film information, including details like event IDs, names, descriptions, URLs, and pass information for your film festival schedule.

All requests to the Eventive API must include the Content-Type: application/json header.

תוצאות החיפוש עבור פסטיבל תמר 2026:

פסטיבל התמר ישוב במהדורתו ה-26 ויתקיים בחול המועד סוכות, בין התאריכים 28 בספטמבר ל-2 באוקטובר 2026, למשך חמישה ימים של הופעות חיות.

**לוח הופעות:**

חגיגת הפתיחה שייערכו בהיכל מצדה ב-28 בספטמבר יובילו מארינה מקסימיליאן, מופעים משותפים של מירי מסיקה וקרן פלס וגם של אברהם טל ומוש בן ארי, ואתניקס.

בערב השני, 29 בספטמבר, יופיעו על אותה הבמה פול טראנק, דודו טסה, שרית חדד, רביד פלוטניק ופטרה.

ב-30 בספטמבר יופיעו ברי סחרוף, נגה ארז, אודיה וטונה, ובערב האחרון, 1 באוקטובר, יעלו על הבמה ג'ימבו ג'יי, לירן דנינו, היהודים, בן צור ועדן בן זקן.

**הופעות פתוחות:**

בקיבוץ עין גדי יופיעו מני בגר (29 בספטמבר) וגל דה פז (30 בספטמבר). בפארק נחל אמציהו ביישובי כיכר סדום יופיעו עלמה גוב (30 בספטמבר) ושאזאמאט (1 באוקטובר).

מחיר כרטיס לערב אחד של הופעות נע בין 289 שקלים ל-369 שקלים.

- **Red Sea Jazz Festival** (music-jazz), Eilat, 11–14 Nov 2026. Programme at https://redseajazz.co.il/ (the "לוח זמנים" block). Ticketing is Ticketmaster.co.il. Evidence: "The 3 Cohens · Port arena · 12.11 · 20:00".
- **TLVFest** (film-lgbtq), Tel Aviv Cinematheque, 22–31 Oct 2026. The programme is on the Cinematheque site at https://www.cinema.co.il/תכנית-הפסטיבל/, not on tlvfest.com, which has nothing for 2026 yet. Ticketing is the Cinematheque's own system (cintlv.pres.global). Evidence: "18:00 22/10/2026 / אולם 2" (the film עורבים).
- **Challenge ISRAMAN 2027** (sports-triathlon), Eilat, 27–30 Jan 2027. The full weekend schedule and start-wave table are at https://israman.co.il/?page_id=313. Evidence: "06:10 CHALLENGE ISRAMAN 226 Elite …"; the snippet I kept does not show which day that is.

**Partial:**
- **Jerusalem Marathon**, 19 Mar 2027: the races are listed and the event runs "06:00-14:00", but per-race start times aren't out.
- **Tel Aviv Marathon**, 26 Feb 2027: only the kids' race time is published (24.02 at 16:00, HaYarkon Park).
- **Tamar Festival**, 28 Sep – 2 Oct 2026, Masada and the Dead Sea: nightly lineups only, no session times on the site; times are on Ticketmaster. Only its last two days fall in the window.

**Expected, with next-edition dates:**
- **Soundtrack Festival** (new lead), Tel Aviv Cinematheque, 24–28 Nov 2026.
- **Eilat Chamber Music Festival**, mid-Nov 2026 per Tourist Israel. The site still shows the 2025 edition. It is a Wix page with sessions in the raw HTML, and tickets are on GoShow.
- **Piano Festival**, which has moved to Eilat, around New Year 2027. Tickets on Ticketmaster.
- **Jerusalem Jewish Film Festival**, Jerusalem Cinematheque, 13–18 Dec 2026.
- **Jacob's Ladder**, now at Kfar Blum over 31 Dec 2026 – 2 Jan 2027, no longer Ginosar in May. The programme is a PDF, and tickets are on ticks.co.il.
- **Jerusalem International Chamber Music Festival**, YMCA, early Sep 2027.
- **Summer 2027:** the Israel Festival and Jerusalem Jazz Festival, Karmiel, Docaviv, the student film festival (TISFF), Hutzot Hayotzer and Animix. Where I checked the last edition's programme pages (Israel Festival, Karmiel, TISFF, JCMF), they were server-rendered.
- **Tel Aviv Jazz Festival**, said to be mid-Dec 2026, but I found no official site. **Genesis** is expected in May 2027 and **Meteor** in Sep 2027; neither has been checked.

**Discovery routes:**
- **Cinematheque festival index** (https://www.cinema.co.il/פסטיבלים/) gave the best yield. TLVFest, Soundtrack, Animix, the children's festival and the Docaviv and TISFF screenings all use the same page layout ("HH:MM DD/MM/YYYY / אולם N"), so one parser could cover about five festivals.
- **Tourist Israel and iTravelJerusalem** are reliable for dates.
- **mevalim.co.il/festivals/** is good for leads but its session tables are wrong; its Genesis page listed unrelated Caesarea concerts.
- **Guessed domains:** a proxy 502 meant the domain does not exist. Twelve guesses failed that way, including Curtain Up, Intimadance, Hutzot Hayotzer, Kfar Blum, Voice of Music, Animix, Jerusalem Design Week and Tel Aviv Jazz.
- **Blocked or dead routes:** jer-cin.org.il and jff.org.il return 403 to curl, though WebFetch can read jer-cin. The eventer.co.il search URL is a 404, and the Hebrew Wikipedia list title I tried does not exist.

**Rejected or not found:**
- No 2026 dates found for Curtain Up or Intimadance, and nothing at all for Clickerfest.
- The Tel Aviv Piano Festival and "Jacob's Ladder, Ginosar, May" leads are both outdated (the festivals moved).
- Israel Opera is a season, not a festival.
- Seret is not an Israeli festival.

Not researched within the budget: Jerusalem Design Week, Voice of Music, Hebrew Book Week, Jerusalem Film Festival, Masada opera, Ein Gev, Boombamela, the Book Forum, Pride and beer festivals.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about the Spektrix API v3 events endpoint:

## Spektrix Festival API v3 Events

You can pull a full list of all Events that have instances set as "Visible" to Web using the endpoint https://system.spektrix.com/{{clientname}}/api/v3/events.

### Key Features:

**Getting Event Details:**
The GET v3/events/{id} endpoint returns the details of a specific event.

**Filtering Parameters:**
You can use various parameters like instanceStart_from, instanceStart_to, onSale, name, and custom attributes to filter events. The $expand parameter can reveal additional resources like RelatedEvents and RelatedStockItems.

**Creating Events:**
You can create Events using the API v3 System Owner mode early-access endpoint, which is available only to integrations authenticated in API v3 System Owner mode.

**Event Instances:**
Passing the returned Event ID into the v3/events{{id}}/instances endpoint will return all visible instances for that specific event.

The API is designed for festivals and events, supporting various use cases for retrieving and managing event information.

- **id: findarace** | Findarace | https://findarace.com/marathons | aggregator | running, triathlon, multi-distance events | UK | reachable: 200 (301) | per-session: partial | machine-readable: **JSON-LD `SportsEvent`** (40 per page, with `validFrom` for offers) | how-to-use: scrape JSON-LD per category page. | examples: Chelmsford Marathon and Half (Oct 2026).

- **id: wikicfp** | WikiCFP | http://www.wikicfp.com/cfp/ | aggregator | academic, incl. arts, music and film studies | worldwide | reachable: 200 | per-session: no (CFP stage) | machine-readable: **RSS** `http://www.wikicfp.com/cfp/rss?cat=<topic>` (application/xml) | how-to-use: RSS per category (music, film, theatre, art), then check the conference site for a timetable later. | examples: ICSC 2026 (International Csound Conference); cDf Congress 2026 (Barcelona).

## C. Israel-specific aggregators

- **id: il-listing-sites** | Mevalim, LIVE/Tickchak, TicketSI, Makore, Festivalim | https://www.mevalim.co.il/festivals/, https://live.tickchak.co.il/festivals-in-israel, https://www.ticketsi.co.il/, https://www.makore.co.il/, https://festivalim.co.il/ | aggregator | all types | **Israel** | reachable: all 200 | per-session: no | none | how-to-use: harvest festival names, then fingerprint the ticketing platform on each festival's own site (technique T3). | examples: Israel Festival (Jerusalem, May–June 2027).
- **id: itraveljerusalem / visit-tel-aviv** | city tourism calendars | https://www.itraveljerusalem.com, https://www.visit-tel-aviv.com | aggregator | all | Israel | reachable: 200 / 200 (the tel-aviv.gov.il homepage 302s to 200; its EventsList page 404s) | per-session: no | none | examples: Israel Festival 2026 page.

## D. Seed lists (Wikipedia)

Wikimedia's API returns **429 "too many requests"** after a few fast calls. Send a descriptive User-Agent and sleep about 3 seconds between calls, or parse the category HTML.
- **id: wiki-lists** | en.wikipedia list pages | seed-list | 200: List_of_film_festivals, List_of_music_festivals, List_of_fringe_festivals, List_of_literary_festivals, List_of_theatre_festivals, List_of_jazz_festivals, List_of_electronic_music_festivals, List_of_multi-sport_events, List_of_marathon_races, List_of_science_fiction_conventions, Comedy_festival, Category:Comedy_festivals, Category:Dance_festivals, Category:Academic_conferences. **404:** List_of_festivals_in_Israel, List_of_comedy_festivals, List_of_dance_festivals, List_of_art_biennials, List_of_biennials, Category:Biennales.
- **id: wiki-israel-cats** | Israel categories | seed-list | Israel | Category:Festivals_in_Israel lists only subcategories. The useful members are:
  - Film: Haifa IFF, ICon, Rehovot Women's FF, Jerusalem FF, Lethal Lesbian, TAU Student FF, TLVFest.
  - Music: Abu Ghosh, Arabesque, Boombamela, Doof, InDnegev, Safed Klezmer, Pic.Nic. The category also links a page named "List of music festivals in Israel".
  - Tel Aviv: Docaviv, ICon, Pride, Theatronetto, TLVFest, Culture of Peace.
  - Jerusalem: Israel Festival, Festival of Light, JFF, Book Forum, Oud Festival, Opus.
  - he.wikipedia's `קטגוריה:פסטיבלים_בישראל` hit the same 429 and was not read.
- examples of new Israeli candidates for Oct 2026–Sep 2027:
  - **ICon festival** (Tel Aviv, Sukkot Oct 2026; iconfestival.org.il 200; the convention runs a per-session programme)
  - **Docaviv** (May 2027)
  - **Jerusalem Film Festival** (July 2027; jff.org.il **403**)
  - **TLVFest** (tlvfest.com 200)

## E. Techniques

- **id: tenant-config-scrape** | technique | read a SaaS tenant's bootstrap config (Eventive `TENANT`, Sched `all.ics`, Indico export, pretalx schedule.json) instead of the rendered page. This gets past HTML 403s: Sched HTML 403s while its ICS returns 200.
- **id: ticketing-fingerprint** | technique | fetch a candidate's homepage and grep the outbound links for known platforms (`eventive.org|sched.com|pretalx|indico|spektrix|eventotron|eventer.co.il|ticketmaster.co.il|smarticket|tixwise|pretix|eventact|clashfinder`). This was verified on 11 Israeli festival sites: Tamar, Red Sea Jazz and Piano were Ticketmaster IL; Suzanne Dellal was Smarticket; Other Israel was Eventive; Karmiel and Animix run their own `/events/` pages. A platform hit implies a per-session schedule.
- **id: site-queries** | search-query | the useful site: queries were:
  - `site:eventive.org schedule 2027`
  - `site:sched.com 2027 festival`
  - `site:pretix.eu festival 2027`
  - `site:eventact.com program 2027`
  - `site:program.eventact.com`
  - `site:indico.global timetable 2027`
  - `site:clashfinder.com/m/ 2027`
  - `site:eventer.co.il פסטיבל 2027`
  - `"system.spektrix.com" festival`
  - Sched and Israel returned only old (2013–2018) hits.
- **id: platform-global-lists** | technique | some platforms publish their whole tenant list: pretalx `/api/events/` (739), World Fringe WP REST (255), Indico `export/categ/0.json` by date window, RunSignup `/Rest/races`. Sweep these first; they enumerate without a search engine.

## Best 10 techniques, ranked

1. **pretalx global event list.** `GET pretalx.com/api/events/` then `/<slug>/schedule/export/schedule.json`. It covers conferences completely and every hit has a per-session schedule.
2. **Eventive tenant scrape.** Search `site:eventive.org schedule`, read the `TENANT` api_key and bucket, then `api.eventive.org/event_buckets/<b>/events`. This gives per-screening JSON for film festivals.
3. **Sched ICS.** Search `site:sched.com 2027` and fetch `<slug>.sched.com/all.ics`. The HTML is 403 but the ICS works. Covers film, comedy, conventions and conferences.
4. **Ticketing fingerprint on seed lists.** Take names from Wikipedia, World Fringe and Israeli listing sites, then grep each homepage for a known platform. This is the main Israel route: Ticketmaster IL, Smarticket, Eventer, Eventact.
5. **World Fringe WP REST.** 255 fringes with links; diff them against the registry. Every fringe is per-show by nature.
6. **Indico category export by date window.** Sweep indico.global, indico.cern.ch and university instances. Covers academic events, incl. Israeli physics.
7. **Eventact / Ortra for Israeli conferences.** Ortra's homepage lists them; the agendas are on `program.eventact.com`. Example: AIS Oct 19–21 2026, Ramat Gan.
8. **RunSignup API for race weekends.** Rank by events per race and days spanned. Example: Disney Marathon Weekend, Jan 2027. For Israel, Israman (Eilat, Jan 27–30 2027) comes from a direct search; ahotu and worldsmarathons are 403.
9. **The Comic's Comic monthly calendar for comedy**, then check each festival for Sched, Eventotron or its own schedule.
10. **Clashfinder for music running orders.** It has the best per-stage set times, but it needs a free account and API key, and the captcha blocks it here. Use Songkick, JamBase and EDMtrain only for names.

NOT FOUND or not done within budget:
- dance-specific aggregators (dance-europe returned 502)
- the literature aggregator contents
- Spektrix client enumeration
- the Whova public agenda (app-gated)
- Tixwise, Zappa and go-out (blocked)
- the Israeli Ministry of Culture festival list (403)
- a JSON behind Eventer categories
- Elevent (526)
- Tessitura

Aggregators mostly give names and dates only, and many are blocked (403). For Israel, the reliable route is to check which ticketing platform a festival's own site links to.

**Platforms where a hosted festival has a per-session schedule**
- **pretalx** (tech and academic conferences, Europe-heavy): `GET https://pretalx.com/api/events/` returns every hosted event with no key. Today that was 739 events, 87 starting on or after 2026-10-01. Each one has `/<slug>/schedule/export/schedule.json` (checked: 200).
  - Examples: Hack.lu (20 Oct 2026), PyConES (6 Nov 2026), Texas Linux Fest (6 Nov 2026).
- **Eventive** (film festivals): I pulled a real schedule this way.
  - Each festival's `/<slug>.<hash>.js` sets a `TENANT` object with a public `api_key` and an `event_bucket`.
  - `https://api.eventive.org/event_buckets/<bucket>/events?api_key=<key>` then returns JSON screenings with start times and venues. Portland Film Festival 2026 returned 63 events, 62 with dates.
  - Find festivals with `site:eventive.org schedule 2027`.
  - Examples: Portland FF (from 1 Oct 2026), Other Israel Film Festival (New York, November; Israel-related), Raindance (London, June 2027).
- **Sched** (conferences, comedy, film, conventions): the web pages return 403, but `https://<slug>.sched.com/all.ics` returns 200 with a full calendar (140 events for Sidewalk Film Festival).
  - Find festivals with `site:sched.com 2027 festival`.
  - Examples: ConVocation 2027 (20–21 Feb 2027), the CDS Annual Conference (3–6 Nov 2026), and probably SF Sketchfest in January 2027.
  - Searching Sched for Israeli events found only 2013–2018 ones.
- **Indico** (academic):
  - `/export/categ/<id>.json?from=&to=` works on indico.global. On indico.cern.ch the export of the root category timed out, so ask in date windows.
  - `/category/<id>/events.ics` also works on both.
  - Example: Israel Joint Particle Physics Meetings (indico.global category 1193).
- **Eventact / Ortra** (Israeli conferences): ortra.com's homepage lists upcoming Israeli conferences, and the agendas are on `program.eventact.com`. There is no JSON; agendas are HTML or PDF.
  - Example: AIS 2026, the Association for Israel Studies conference, 19–21 Oct 2026 in Ramat Gan, with sessions by hall.
- **RunSignup** (race weekends, mostly US): `https://runsignup.com/Rest/races?format=json&events=T&start_date=…` needs no key, and each race lists its events with start times.
  - Ranking races by number of events finds the festival-like weekends.
  - Example: Walt Disney World Marathon Weekend, 7–10 Jan 2027.
- **Partial or not verified:**
  - **pretix:** an organiser's calendar is at `https://pretix.eu/<org>/events/ical/`.
  - **Ticketmaster Israel:** one event code per show. The Tamar Festival at Masada (Sukkot, October 2026), Red Sea Jazz Eilat and the Eilat Piano Festival sell through it.
  - **Smarticket:** used by Suzanne Dellal (Tel Aviv dance).
  - **Spektrix:** you can find a festival's client name by searching its HTML for `system.spektrix.com/<client>`. I found no new examples.
  - **Clashfinder:** has the best per-stage music set times, but a captcha blocks both curl and WebFetch, and its API needs a free account and key.
  - **Eventer category pages:** the page is script-rendered, so I found no JSON behind it. Use `site:eventer.co.il פסטיבל 2027` to get producer slugs for the adapter you already have.

**Aggregators and seed lists**
- **World Fringe:** its WordPress feed `worldfringe.com/wp-json/wp/v2/fringe-festival` lists 255 fringes with links but no dates. Compare it against the registry.
- **The Comic's Comic:** a comedy calendar by month, with dates and cities.
  - Examples: Galway (20–26 Oct 2026), New York Comedy Festival (6–15 Nov 2026), Just For Laughs Sydney (9–22 Nov 2026).
- **findarace:** UK races, with structured sports-event data embedded in each page.
- **WikiCFP:** an RSS feed per topic.
- **The tech-conferences GitHub data:** conference JSON files by year and topic.
- **Wikipedia seed lists:**
  - The film, music, fringe, literary, theatre and jazz list pages exist.
  - "List of festivals in Israel", comedy, dance and art biennials all return 404.
  - Israeli subcategories give new candidates: ICon (Tel Aviv, Sukkot October 2026), Docaviv (May 2027), Jerusalem Film Festival (July 2027; its site returns 403) and TLVFest.
  - Wikipedia rate-limits fast requests (429), so space them about 3 seconds apart.
- **Blocked today:**
  - Music: FilmFreeway, musicfestivalwizard, festicket, bandsintown, lineups.com, ra.co.
  - Conferences: 10times.
  - Sports: ahotu and worldsmarathons (their calendar pages).
  - Israel: tixwise, zappa, the gov.il culture pages and jerusalem.muni.il.
  - go-out.co.il resets the connection, and Eventbrite returns 429.

4. Take names from seed lists (Wikipedia, World Fringe, Israeli listing sites) and search each festival's homepage for links to a known ticketing platform. This is the main route for Israel. I checked 11 Israeli sites this way; eight showed a platform link or their own events pages.
5. Compare World Fringe's 255 entries against the registry.
6. Sweep Indico instances by date window.
7. Use Ortra and Eventact for Israeli conferences.
8. Use the RunSignup API for race weekends. Israman (Eilat, 27–30 Jan 2027) came from a direct search, since the running calendars are blocked.
9. Use The Comic's Comic calendar for comedy, then look for each festival's schedule platform.
10. Use Clashfinder for music running orders once an account exists; use Songkick, JamBase and EDMtrain for names only.

**Not found within the budget:** dance aggregators (dance-europe returned 502), what the literature aggregators actually list, Spektrix client examples, public Whova agendas (they sit behind the app), the Israeli Ministry of Culture festival list (403), Elevent (526) and Tessitura.

# Academic conferences in Israel, 2026-10-01 to 2027-09-30, with per-session programmes

Researched 2026-09-29, about 55 tool calls. ISRA 2026 was skipped because it is already in the product.

**Main finding:** **EventAct** is the platform to target. Its open API gives a per-session timetable (day, start, end, hall) through the same widget pattern the ISRA adapter already uses (`<ea-program event= agenda= key=>` then `GET https://api.eventact.com/o/v2/agenda/<event>/<agenda>/en/timetable` with header `API-Token: <key>`). Two further EventAct facts:
- **`agenda="0"` works.** The API then resolves the event's default agenda (seen on MPN2027).
- **The widget can sit on either page type.** Some programme pages carry it themselves. Others (AIS) only link out to `program.eventact.com/Program/<code>/<code>/en`, and the widget is on that page.

## 1. Candidates

| Name | Organiser | Discipline (slug) | City + venue | Dates | Programme URL | Per-session status | Platform | Machine-readable endpoint | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **42nd AIS Conference: "Security, Rehabilitation and Healing"** | Association for Israel Studies (EventAct company "AIS") | academic-israel-studies (social sciences/humanities) | Ramat Gan, Ramat Gan Academic College | 19–21 Oct 2026 | https://ws.eventact.com/AIS2026/Program → https://program.eventact.com/Program/iOZQAAA/iozk/en | **published** (106 activities, 3 days, Hall 1–11) | eventact | `api.eventact.com/o/v2/agenda/37945/14755/en/timetable`, header `API-Token: 50a7ed9768604ff2bef20dc2914469df`; per-session detail at `/o/v2/agenda/37945/<id>/session` | "(MA-01) Peace, Conflict and Media Narratives in Israeli Society", 19 Oct 09:00–10:30, Hall 1. PDF timetable also available (`AIS_2026_Final_Conference_Program_with_Timetable_25-09-26_B.pdf`) |
| **72nd Annual Meeting, Israel Physical Society** (expected) | IPS (host university rotates) | academic-physics | TBA (71st was at HUJI Givat Ram) | expected ~June/July 2027 (71st: 1 Jul 2026, 70th: 15 Jul 2025) | https://www.israelphysicalsociety.org/conferences (pattern `/conference/<n>th-annual-meeting/program`) | **not-yet-published**, very likely: the 71st had a full per-talk HTML schedule with rooms | custom (server-rendered HTML) | none found; scrape the HTML | 71st: "AMO Ia: Quantum Devices…", 14:00, Sprinzak 115; review talk 11:15–11:55, Canada hall |

| **JEMAC 2026** | Paragon (EventAct company 2254) | academic-medicine (emergency medicine; worth confirming) | Jerusalem, ICC | 12–13 Nov 2026 | https://ws.eventact.com/JEMAC2026 | **not-yet-published**: widget present, timetable empty | eventact | `/o/v2/agenda/38601/14914/en/timetable`, key `74d45827f3f14e69a914d4b3af98b169` (currently `tables: []`) | Worth re-polling. The widget is already wired |
| **MPN 2027** | Paragon | academic-medicine (hematology, myeloproliferative neoplasms) | Tel Aviv, Hilton | 18 Feb 2027 | https://ws.eventact.com/mpn2027/Program | **not-yet-published**: the agenda still holds the 2026 edition (16 Apr 2026, "Main hall") | eventact | `/o/v2/agenda/37988/0/en/timetable`, key `3aff77c616064315bbd745bc00268dc1` | Single hall, one day. Low value |
| **NANO.IL.2027 · ICS 90** (joint nanotech + 90th Israel Chemical Society meeting, as listed) | Paragon / HUJI | academic-chemistry / academic-nanotech | Jerusalem, ICC | 14–15 Feb 2027 | http://nanoilconf.com/ (503, "under maintenance") | **not-yet-published**, likely: multi-hall, and past ICS meetings used Bizzabo or custom sites with halls | unknown (possibly eventact, since Paragon runs it) | none yet | Dates come from Paragon's EventAct listing |
| **ISPHO 2026** | Comtec (EventAct company 70) | academic-medicine (paediatric haemato-oncology) | Ma'alot-Tarshiha, Hacienda Forest View hotel | 29–31 Oct 2026 | https://ws.eventact.com/ispho | **unknown**: the site nav is JS-rendered and no widget was found on the home page | eventact | — | Check the programme subpage next time |
| **Psychedelic Medicine – Israel** | Comtec | academic-medicine (psychiatry) | Israel (venue not listed) | 19–21 Oct 2026 | https://www.psychmedisrael.com/ | **unknown** (no programme link found) | custom | — | — |

Smaller one-day medical meetings on the same PCO lists are left out of the table because they are single-track days rarely worth a planner. They are: the Poultry Science conference (1–3 Nov, Nazareth, PDF-only programme), the Wolfson neuromuscular conference, the Sheba liver-disease study day, ENT paediatrics, the coagulation society, ISHLA 2027, the Auditory Research day, and several obstetrics/gynaecology branch meetings. They can be re-surfaced from the same API calls.

Known ids: Ortra 12, Comtec 70, Paragon 2254, Target 1899, Technion 2332, TAU 572, Dan 75. The last four returned nothing upcoming. Paging beyond page 1 returned nothing. `Kenes`, `Unitours`, `Eshet` and `IMA` are not EventAct company names |
| **EventAct agenda API** | `GET https://api.eventact.com/o/v2/agenda/<event>/<agenda>/en/timetable` + `API-Token` | 200 | AIS 2026 full timetable | Read the widget from `<ea-program>` on the programme page or on the `program.eventact.com/Program/...` page it links to. `agenda=0` resolves to the default agenda. An empty `tables` means not yet published. Check the `startDate` year for stale agendas |
| Ortra calendar | https://eng.ortra.com/calendar/y2026/ (`/y2027/` returns 404) | 200 | Confirmed the Ortra list | Human-readable. Covers the same events as the API |

# Festival discovery sources, probed 2026-09-29

The HTTP codes come from curl through the sandbox proxy today. A 403 means blocked, so it was not retried. Codes marked "->" followed a redirect.
The project already has adapters for Eventotron (Brighton, Leicester), Spektrix v3 (EIF, Book Festival) and Eventer producer pages (Acco). This list only adds to them.

## A. Platforms: a festival hosted here has a per-session schedule by construction

- **id: eventive** | Eventive (film festivals) | https://eventive.org | platform | film, some doc and shorts festivals | mostly US, CA and UK, plus diaspora festivals | reachable: 200 (api.eventive.org 200) | per-session: **yes** | machine-readable: **yes, verified.** Each tenant page `https://<slug>.eventive.org/schedule` loads `/<slug>.<hash>.js`. That script sets `TENANT = {..."api_key":"<public key>","event_bucket":"<id>"}`. Then `GET https://api.eventive.org/event_buckets/<bucket>/events?api_key=<key>` returns JSON events with `start_time`, `venue.name` and `films`.   - Tel Aviv: Docaviv, ICon, Pride, Theatronetto, TLVFest, Culture of Peace.
  - Jerusalem: Israel Festival, Festival of Light, JFF, Book Forum, Oud Festival, Opus.
  - he.wikipedia's `קטגוריה:פסטיבלים_בישראל` hit the same 429 and was not read.
- examples of new Israeli candidates for Oct 2026–Sep 2027:
  - **ICon festival** (Tel Aviv, Sukkot Oct 2026; iconfestival.org.il 200; the convention runs a per-session programme)
  - **Docaviv** (May 2027)
  - **Jerusalem Film Festival** (July 2027; jff.org.il **403**)
  - **TLVFest** (tlvfest.com 200)

## E. Techniques

- **id: tenant-config-scrape** | technique | read a SaaS tenant's bootstrap config (Eventive `TENANT`, Sched `all.ics`, Indico export, pretalx schedule.json) instead of the rendered page. This gets past HTML 403s: Sched HTML 403s while its ICS returns 200.
- **id: ticketing-fingerprint** | technique | fetch a candidate's homepage and grep the outbound links for known platforms (`eventive.org|sched.com|pretalx|indico|spektrix|eventotron|eventer.co.il|ticketmaster.co.il|smarticket|tixwise|pretix|eventact|clashfinder`). This was verified on 11 Israeli festival sites: Tamar, Red Sea Jazz and Piano were Ticketmaster IL; Suzanne Dellal was Smarticket; Other Israel was Eventive; Karmiel and Animix run their own `/events/` pages. A platform hit implies a per-session schedule.
- **id: site-queries** | search-query | the useful site: queries were:
  - `site:eventive.org schedule 2027`
  - `site:sched.com 2027 festival`
  - `site:pretix.eu festival 2027`
  - `site:eventact.com program 2027`
  - `site:program.eventact.com`
  - `site:indico.global timetable 2027`
  - `site:clashfinder.com/m/ 2027`
  - `site:eventer.co.il פסטיבל 2027`
  - `"system.spektrix.com" festival`
  - Sched and Israel returned only old (2013–2018) hits.
- **id: platform-global-lists** | technique | some platforms publish their whole tenant list: pretalx `/api/events/` (739), World Fringe WP REST (255), Indico `export/categ/0.json` by date window, RunSignup `/Rest/races`. Sweep these first; they enumerate without a search engine.

## Best 10 techniques, ranked

1. **pretalx global event list.** `GET pretalx.com/api/events/` then `/<slug>/schedule/export/schedule.json`. It covers conferences completely and every hit has a per-session schedule.
2. **Eventive tenant scrape.** Search `site:eventive.org schedule`, read the `TENANT` api_key and bucket, then `api.eventive.org/event_buckets/<b>/events`. This gives per-screening JSON for film festivals.
3. **Sched ICS.** Search `site:sched.com 2027` and fetch `<slug>.sched.com/all.ics`. The HTML is 403 but the ICS works. Covers film, comedy, conventions and conferences.
4. **Ticketing fingerprint on seed lists.** Take names from Wikipedia, World Fringe and Israeli listing sites, then grep each homepage for a known platform. This is the main Israel route: Ticketmaster IL, Smarticket, Eventer, Eventact.
5. **World Fringe WP REST.** 255 fringes with links; diff them against the registry. Every fringe is per-show by nature.
6. **Indico category export by date window.** Sweep indico.global, indico.cern.ch and university instances. Covers academic events, incl. Israeli physics.
7. **Eventact / Ortra for Israeli conferences.** Ortra's homepage lists them; the agendas are on `program.eventact.com`. Example: AIS Oct 19–21 2026, Ramat Gan.
8. **RunSignup API for race weekends.** Rank by events per race and days spanned. Example: Disney Marathon Weekend, Jan 2027. For Israel, Israman (Eilat, Jan 27–30 2027) comes from a direct search; ahotu and worldsmarathons are 403.
9. **The Comic's Comic monthly calendar for comedy**, then check each festival for Sched, Eventotron or its own schedule.
10. **Clashfinder for music running orders.** It has the best per-stage set times, but it needs a free account and API key, and the captcha blocks it here. Use Songkick, JamBase and EDMtrain only for names.

NOT FOUND or not done within budget:
- dance-specific aggregators (dance-europe returned 502)
- the literature aggregator contents
- Spektrix client enumeration
- the Whova public agenda (app-gated)
- Tixwise, Zappa and go-out (blocked)
- the Israeli Ministry of Culture festival list (403)
- a JSON behind Eventer categories
- Elevent (526)
- Tessitura

[[source]]
id = "eventact"
name = "EventAct (the platform behind Ortra, Comtec, Paragon and most Israeli conference organisers)"
category = "platform"
url = "https://ws.eventact.com"
kinds = ["academic"]
regions = ["IL"]
per_session = "yes"
machine_readable = "POST https://ws.eventact.com/api/EventsApi/EventListInfo {CompanyId, Lang: 9, SearchType: 1, PageIndex: 1, PageSize: 100} lists a company's upcoming events; GET https://api.eventact.com/o/v2/agenda/<event>/<agenda>/en/timetable with header API-Token: <key> is one event's timetable (day, start, end, hall)"
how = """List each organiser's upcoming events: company ids Ortra 12, Comtec 70, Paragon 2254 (Target 1899, Technion 2332, TAU 572, Dan 75 had none upcoming on 2026-09-29); a new organiser's id is the initList(<id>, …) on ws.eventact.com/c/<Name>. \
For each event, the programme page (or the program.eventact.com/Program/<code>/<code>/en page it links to) carries <ea-program event= agenda= key=>; agenda 0 resolves to the default agenda. \
An empty tables list means the programme is not out yet; a startDate in last year's edition means the agenda was not rolled over. \
The ISRA adapter already reads this API. Skip one-day single-hall meetings: nothing to plan."""

[[source]]
id = "eventact"
name = "EventAct (the platform behind Ortra, Comtec, Paragon and most Israeli conference organisers)"
category = "platform"
url = "https://ws.eventact.com"
kinds = ["academic"]
regions = ["IL"]
per_session = "yes"
machine_readable = "POST https://ws.eventact.com/api/EventsApi/EventListInfo {CompanyId, Lang: 9, SearchType: 1, PageIndex: 1, PageSize: 100} lists a company's upcoming events; GET https://api.eventact.com/o/v2/agenda/<event>/<agenda>/en/timetable with header API-Token: <key> is one event's timetable (day, start, end, hall)"
how = """List each organiser's upcoming events: company ids Ortra 12, Comtec 70, Paragon 2254 (Target 1899, Technion 2332, TAU 572, Dan 75 had none upcoming on 2026-09-29); a new organiser's id is the initList(<id>, …) on ws.eventact.com/c/<Name>. \
For each event, the programme page (or the program.eventact.com/Program/<code>/<code>/en page it links to) carries <ea-program event= agenda= key=>; agenda 0 resolves to the default agenda. \
An empty tables list means the programme is not out yet; a startDate in last year's edition means the agenda was not rolled over. \
The ISRA adapter already reads this API. Skip one-day single-hall meetings: nothing to plan."""
status = "active"

[[source]]
id = "eventact"
name = "EventAct (the platform behind Ortra, Comtec, Paragon and most Israeli conference organisers)"
category = "platform"
url = "https://ws.eventact.com"
kinds = ["academic"]
regions = ["IL"]
per_session = "yes"
machine_readable = "POST https://ws.eventact.com/api/EventsApi/EventListInfo {CompanyId, Lang: 9, SearchType: 1, PageIndex: 1, PageSize: 100} lists a company's upcoming events; GET https://api.eventact.com/o/v2/agenda/<event>/<agenda>/en/timetable with header API-Token: <key> is one event's timetable (day, start, end, hall)"
how = """List each organiser's upcoming events: company ids Ortra 12, Comtec 70, Paragon 2254 (Target 1899, Technion 2332, TAU 572, Dan 75 had none upcoming on 2026-09-29); a new organiser's id is the initList(<id>, …) on ws.eventact.com/c/<Name>. \
For each event, the programme page (or the program.eventact.com/Program/<code>/<code>/en page it links to) carries <ea-program event= agenda= key=>; agenda 0 resolves to the default agenda. \
An empty tables list means the programme is not out yet; a startDate in last year's edition means the agenda was not rolled over. \
The ISRA adapter already reads this API. Skip one-day single-hall meetings: nothing to plan."""

# Finder run, 2026-09-29

The first run, which also set the lists up. Scope: academic conferences worldwide with Israel
first, the discovery method for every kind, and Israeli festivals of every kind from
October 2026 to September 2027. Three research passes worked in parallel.

## What each route yielded

- **eventact** (Israeli conference organisers): 15 upcoming Israeli events across Ortra,
  Comtec and Paragon, one with a published per-session timetable (the Association for Israel
  Studies conference, 106 sessions in 11 halls). Its agenda API is the one ISRA already uses.
- **pretalx**: 87 hosted events from October 2026 on, all fetched in one call. Of the few
  schedules fetched, Hack.lu, PyConES and MarxismNL are published; the academic societies'
  (World History Association, DVRW, Africa Bioethics, ANZSOC) answer 404 until release.
- **tel-aviv-cinematheque**: TLVFest's programme is live there (not on tlvfest.com), plus
  the Soundtrack, Animix and children's festivals on the same template.
- **ticketing-fingerprint**: a platform link on 8 of 11 Israeli festival sites; Red Sea Jazz
  and the Eilat Piano Festival sell on Ticketmaster Israel.
- **Hebrew and English searches**: Israman's full race weekend, the Tel Aviv and Jerusalem
  marathons, the Israel Physical Society meeting.
- **Nothing**: Indico (no Israeli events upcoming), conferenceindex (paper-mill listings),
  science.co.il (stale), HUJI IIAS (one-day workshops), the IMA events page (archive only),
  the eventer.co.il search URL (404), twelve guessed Israeli festival domains (none exist).

## Leads not yet recorded as candidates

Each lacks an official site to point at; find one first.

- Tel Aviv Jazz Festival: mid-December 2026 per Tourist Israel; no official site found.
- Genesis Festival, Ma'ayan Harod: mid-May 2027; official site not checked.
- Meteor Festival, Lehavot HaBashan: 6 to 8 Sep 2027 per one guide.
- Israeli Association for Group Guidance and Therapy conference, Rabin Center, 15 to 17 Feb
  2027: its site answered with a bot challenge.
- Mevalim leads: Theatronetto, Jerusalem East and West, Lumagica, Kinneret Vibes, Bein
  HaKramim, Breeza, Rokenrola.

## Next run, first

- Recheck the watched candidates due (`finder.py --report`), JEMAC and ISPHO first.
- Sweep every pretalx schedule in the window, and Eventive and Sched by site: search.
- Israeli societies not yet tried: microbiology, cancer research, ecology, philosophy,
  political science, sociology, the medical specialty societies; and the Kenes Israel list.
- Not reached this run: Jerusalem Design Week, Voice of Music in the Upper Galilee, Hebrew
  Book Week, Jerusalem Film Festival, Ein Gev and Boombamela at Passover, the Jerusalem
  International Book Forum, Hebrew Wikipedia's festival category.
EOF
python3 scraper/finder/finder.py --report | head -60

input.body:
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"missingbulb"} -->
_Requested by **Ariel** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Tkg1DM8zUNirsvzt7nNoyo?thread=cmsg_01Tkg1DM8zUNirsvzt7nNoyo9tsqD9aHdZNqT5ApAyFavr)_

Before: finding festivals was a fresh research pass each time. What a pass learned (which aggregators work, which platforms expose schedules, which festivals were already ruled out) lived in a thread or a handoff note and was lost.

After: `scraper/finder/` keeps two append-only lists. `sources.toml` holds 41 places and ways to look, and `candidates.toml` holds 67 festivals considered: 20 adopted, 8 ready with a published per-session programme, 34 watched with recheck dates, and 5 rejected with reasons. Each run reads both and writes back new candidates and new sources, so the method only grows. A monthly `festival-finder` task runs it, and the `festival-finder` skill is its procedure.

The four stages the owner described, plus the city cycle, are in `docs/data-lifecycle.md`. It maps each stage to where it is built today and names what is not built yet.

**This run's finds with a published per-session programme**
- Association for Israel Studies conference, Ramat Gan, 19–21 Oct: 106 sessions in 11 halls through EventAct's agenda API, the same API the ISRA adapter reads.
- TLVFest, on the Tel Aviv Cinematheque site, 22–31 Oct.
- Red Sea Jazz, Eilat, 11–14 Nov.
- Challenge Israman, Eilat, 27–30 Jan 2027.
- Hack.lu, PyConES and the MarxismNL conference, via pretalx.
- The Walt Disney World Marathon Weekend, via RunSignup.

**The strongest techniques recorded**
- EventAct's event-list API, one call per Israeli conference organiser.
- pretalx's global event list.
- Eventive's tenant config.
- Sched's `all.ics` (it works where the HTML returns 403).
- The Tel Aviv Cinematheque's festival index, one template shared by about five film festivals.
- Fingerprinting a festival site's ticketing platform.

**How**
- `finder.py --check` validates both lists and requires every festival registered under `scraper/festivals/` to have an adopted candidate.
- `--growth origin/main` fails a change that drops an entry since the branch left main. Entries are retired with a status, never deleted.
- `verify.sh` runs both checks. The CI `ci` job now checks out full history so the growth check has main to compare against.
- `npm run verify` passes locally.

**Academic conferences:** Most Israeli conferences are run by a few conference organisers (Ortra, Comtec, Paragon) on one ticketing and programme platform, EventAct. - **Association for Israel Studies conference**, Ramat Gan, 19–21 Oct: 106 sessions across 11 halls (I checked the API response myself).
- **Hack.lu, PyConES and a MarxismNL conference** abroad, found through pretalx, a conference-scheduling site whose event list is open to anyone.

Waiting for their programmes: the Israel Society for Neuroscience meeting (Eilat, January), NANO.IL with the Israel Chemical Society's meeting (February), the Israel Physical Society meeting (summer) and a few medical meetings.

**Other types, ready now:** TLVFest (its programme is on the Tel Aviv Cinematheque site, not its own), Red Sea Jazz (Eilat, November) and Challenge Israman (Eilat, January).

**Best new search methods:**
- EventAct's list of each organiser's events, for Israeli conferences.
- pretalx's full event list, for conferences worldwide.
- Eventive, a ticketing site many film festivals use; its data can be read directly.
- Sched's calendar download, which works even though its pages refuse us.
- The Tel Aviv Cinematheque's festival index: about five film festivals use the same page layout, so one scraper could cover all of them.

- Data sources are recorded per festival, not per year, so a festival can't say which sources a given year used.
- Rapid ticket refresh runs for the Edinburgh Fringe only.
- The city cycle covers sights, but not hotels, restaurants or excursions.

# Writing pack prose

Whether a candidate *qualifies* as a rule at all, and which mechanism carries it, is
[extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md)'s call — settle it there before writing.

**Start from the foundation:** read the "Write each rule" section of
[authoring-agent-docs](../../../basics/skills/authoring-agent-docs/SKILL.md) first — its
principles (concrete enough to verify, motivation stated, what to do rather than what not to,
the right altitude, emphasis reserved) bind pack prose too. This skill is the pack-specific
layer on top of them, and doesn't restate them.

## The ration

Every rule in a `RULES.md` is paid for by every session in every repo that declares the pack,
forever, whether or not it ever applies — so prose is rationed, and the ration is small.

- **One sentence per rule, near 40 words**: the trigger, the directive, and a consequence
  clause only where the rule cannot be applied without it. A candidate that needs a paragraph
  to land has not been understood well enough to be a rule yet.
- **An extraction pass adds at most two rules.** If more candidates clear the bar, write the
  two strongest and drop the rest — they will recur if they were real.
- **Split a rule that carries two situations.** Each situation is its own rule with its own
  trigger.
- A `SKILL.md` loads only when its activity is under way, so it may carry procedure at length —
  but it is still rationed by the same test: every line must change what the reader does.
  Method, steps and decision points belong there; anything a session must know *without*
  loading it belongs in `RULES.md` or a check, and rationale belongs on the element's
  provenance file (below).
- **Moving a rule out of `RULES.md` into a skill** — only where the skill's
  `force-load-on-file-edits-paths` covers *every* moment the rule is needed. A skill whose only
  trigger is its description is picked by the model, not the harness, so a rule that must fire at
  a moment no file edit predicts stays prose, however activity-shaped it reads.
- **Starting a `SKILL.md`, or editing one that declares no body** — say under its frontmatter
  `metadata` what the body is: `body: workflow` for a procedure, whose steps and their gotchas
  change as one, or `body: guidelines` for rules behind a trigger, kept on the skill's one file
  until one has a history of its own. A skill that mixes the two declares the shape of its
  greater part. The harness ignores the key; the corpus's own maintenance reads it, and never
  infers it.

## Shape a rule so it fires

- **Keying a rule to its trigger** — open with the act the reader is performing, not the state
  of the world the rule applies to. Nobody notices that "a value is unknown"; they notice they
  are writing an encoder. A rule keyed to a state never fires, because nothing brings the
  reader to it.
- **Keying a rule the reader reaches while debugging** — name the symptom that sends them
  looking ("A fetch to a host you listed failing in-browser"), not the act that caused it. By
  the time the rule is wanted the act is over, and the symptom is what they can see.
- **Keying a rule that corrects a misconception** — name what the reader wants ("Wanting
  `import`/`export` in extension code"), not the wrong move they might make ("Reaching for a
  bundler"). Someone who doesn't yet know the move is wrong won't recognise themselves in it.
- **Phrasing that trigger** — use the words the reader would use for the situation, and put
  them first and in bold, so the rule is findable by scanning the left margin alone.
- **Choosing the unit** — one block per situation, not one bullet per rule. A reader arrives
  holding a problem, so give them the whole decision in one place rather than a cross-reference
  to three neighbouring bullets.
- **Splitting a rule that only makes sense after the one above it** — don't. If the subject
  needs a "that" pointing back ("Writing that record"), it is a clause of the rule above, not a
  situation of its own. Split when a reader could arrive at the second rule without the first.
- **Separating the blocks** — one blank line between rules. The block is what a reader lands on,
  and an unbroken run of bullets makes them scan lines instead; the separation costs one token.
- **Ordering a file of many rules** — past roughly fifteen, group them under headings naming the
  surface each concerns, so a reader scans headings before subjects. A flat list that long makes
  every bold subject do the work one heading would.
- **Grouping that separates two rules which qualify each other** — add an explicit pointer from
  the general rule to its exception, or the general one reads as unconditional. That pointer is
  the one sentence a rewrite may add that its source didn't have; name it as an addition when
  you report the change.
- **Ordering the clauses** — the default first, then the `if you can't` fallback, then
  `consider` for an optional aid, then the `don't` that the earlier clauses make unnecessary.
- **Choosing modality** — grade it per clause and claim no more than the rule needs. Keep
  `never` and `always` for the genuinely absolute and reach for `prefer`, `avoid` or `rather
  than` otherwise; escalating a `don't` into a `never` changes the rule rather than rewording
  it.
- **Naming a mechanism** — name the check, helper or skill that owns the mechanics, and stop.
  Its parameters, options and failure modes live with it, and restating them here is a copy
  that goes stale. The exception is a mechanism you are telling the reader to *run*, below.
- **Telling the reader to *run* something** — ship the literal invocation in a fenced block, not
  the file's name. The reader is composing a call rather than looking a mechanism up, so a bare
  filename buys a probe every time — the `--help` that prints nothing, then the `cat`, then a
  hand-built command.
- **Closing a block** — say what the other clauses make unnecessary ("don't also comment the
  duplication — the guard covers it"), so nobody adds belt-and-braces.
- **Keeping an exception** — an exception that changes what the reader would do is part of the
  rule; one that only reassures is padding.
- **Cutting a rule's prose** — drop rationale that only restates the rule, examples that
  re-express it, and mechanics another document owns. Keep the motivation itself: a consequence
  the reader needs in order to apply the rule under pressure earns its clause; rationale the
  reader doesn't need at act time goes on the element's provenance file (below).
- **Auditing a file of rules that already exists** — take each rule and ask what a reader would
  get wrong without it. Fold the one whose subject points back at its neighbour; cut the one another
  pack already carries, the one a check now enforces (keeping only the half the check can't see),
  and the one whose mechanism has since been retired — a rule naming code that no longer exists
  teaches a world the reader won't find.
- **Rewriting an existing rule** — carry the source's own strength forward. A rewrite must not
  weaken a rule, and it must not strengthen one either.

## A pack's pitch

- **Knowing who reads a pitch** - a developer whose repository does not run Claudinite, deciding
  from this one paragraph on the claudinite.com dashboard whether the pack is worth adopting. No
  session ever loads it, so it sells the pack rather than instructing anyone.

- **Writing a pitch** - lead with what goes wrong in a repository without the pack, then what
  the pack changes: its main skills by name and the process it runs by itself. Plain and
  concrete, with no hype, no commands, no markdown, no links and no paths, inside the manifest's
  word cap.

- **Counting what a pack carries in its pitch** - in rounded words ("a few", "about a dozen",
  "dozens"), only for the kinds the pack has, never an exact number: the pitch then survives the
  pack's growth, and is rewritten only when what the pack is for changes.

- **Pitching a stub pack** - say it starts empty and is where the repository's own lessons
  about its subject collect; never promise content it does not carry.

## The provenance log - where a rule's rationale lives

A pack keeps one file per element under `provenance/`, beside its `RULES.md`: an append-only
log of the decisions behind the element, read by maintenance and review - the pass that asks
whether a rule still earns its place needs the reason it was written - and never by a session.
No rule sends its reader there, nothing loads it, and it never vendors: a member mounting a
canon pack receives the rules, not the reasoning behind them. The grammar, the kinds, the
fields and the tool are [changing-pack-elements](../changing-pack-elements/SKILL.md)'s; what
this skill adds is how a rule is written so the log can hold it.

- **Ending a rule** - every rule in a `RULES.md` ends with the bare marker naming its file -
  `… never a filesystem walk. (url-filter-host-operators)` - and nothing else: don't name the
  folder, don't link it, don't ask the reader to follow anything. The marker is the element's
  id: two to four hyphenated words for the guideline rather than its wording, chosen once and
  never renamed, so a rewording never touches it and a member's override can name it. Two
  rules whose history is one may share a marker. A guidelines skill's bullets are the skill's
  file's and carry none, until one's history diverges and it takes a marker and a file of its
  own; a workflow skill's steps carry none, the skill being the element.
- **Adding a rule** - write the brief rule and end it with its marker; create its file with a
  `born` entry through `provenance.mjs append` (`mark` creates the file where none exists),
  and put the reason there, never in the rule. A consequence the reader needs under pressure
  earns its clause; rationale the reader doesn't need at act time is the entry's. Write the
  entry so a future review can **reaffirm the rule from it** - `Retire when` is what would
  have to be true for the rule to go.
  - A **workaround** explains the issue with not using it, with the evidence (the failing run,
    the error, the measured cost).
  - A **technology guideline** cites the original documentation it derives from.
  - An **owner decision** carries the language of the request that set it - in a member's
    local pack; a canon file carries the paraphrase, never the quote.
- **Rewording, moving, splitting or converting a rule** - the entry is owed in the same
  change, and the forced skill names its kind.
- **A check's rationale** - on the check's own file, named by its id (`cer/version-bumped` →
  `cer-version-bumped.md`); nothing is added to the check.
- **Removing a rule or check** - its file stays and gains a `retired` entry as its last, in
  the same change.

The `provenance-integrity` check holds the mechanism together - every carrier names a live
file, every file parses - and `provenance-change-recorded` holds the change: a carrier that
changed lands with its entry. A pack not yet on the convention is put there by
`provenance.mjs mark`, and its history filled by the
[backfilling-provenance](../backfilling-provenance/SKILL.md) skill; nothing here is done rule by
rule.

## Evidence

The commit and its PR remain the archive - the story of the incident, quoted exchanges and
session ids live there and in the capture, never in the rule and never in a canon's log. What
an entry takes from them is only the **reaffirmable core**: `Source` and `Reason`, the minimum
a future review needs to re-test the rule, and `Retire when`, the test it is reaffirmed
against. Keep a measurement inline in the rule only where the number *is* the argument - a cost
the reader wouldn't believe stated qualitatively.

# A festival finder run

The finder's files and their fields are `scraper/finder/README.md`; this is how a run works
them. A festival qualifies only when it publishes a detailed per-session schedule: every
show, screening, talk or race with its date, start time and venue.

## Before searching

1. Read the yield of every source, the watched candidates whose recheck date has passed,
   and the candidates ready to adopt:

   ```
   python3 scraper/finder/finder.py --report
   ```

2. Read `candidates.toml` end to end before searching, so a hit is recognised as known
   rather than found twice. Read the last few `runs/` logs for what was tried and came up
   empty.

## The run

## Finishing

10. Check the lists, then open a pull request whose body lists the new candidates with a
    published programme first:

    ```
    python3 scraper/finder/finder.py --check --growth origin/main
    ```

    Adopting a candidate is separate work (stage 2 in `docs/data-lifecycle.md`); when a
    festival is registered under `scraper/festivals/`, its candidate turns `adopted` with
    its `festival_id` in the same change.

# Working with generated files

- **Working with a file a test or tool generates** — put `GENERATED` in its name, and don't
  hand-edit it; change the generator. Never resolve its merge conflict by hand: clear the
  markers with either side, re-run the generator against the merged inputs, and commit that
  output. Consider automating the clear with a `merge=ours` `.gitattributes` entry, and
  `git rerere` for a conflict that recurs.

- **A generator whose OWN set of outputs grows on its own** — one baseline per auto-discovered
  category (a new test "kind", a new fixture), rather than a fixed, named list — needs its
  `merge=ours` coverage to auto-track that growth too, typically a glob or pattern in
  `.gitattributes` rather than one entry per file. A per-file allowlist silently stops covering
  the moment a new category starts committing its own baselines, and the gap surfaces as a
  binary merge conflict git cannot 3-way-merge at all — at the worst possible moment, mid-merge,
  for a category nobody remembered to wire up.

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`); when the change has an issue,
   the body carries `Closes #<issue>` on its own line.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --pr <pr>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --pr <pr>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it
   again. (1)
6. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read an issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.

The merge leaves the local checkout on the branch it squashed, and no step here syncs `main`; the
merge is usually a session's last act. Only if you go on to start further work in this session,
sync first, before branching off anything:

```
git fetch origin main && git checkout main && git reset --hard origin/main && git remote prune origin
```
